name: virel
author: toys-and-building agent
description: Toy block wall, v2 (demo-economy pass; v1 kept as virel.v1.json). CLUE = the object itself, two lines: line 1 is the BOTTOM COURSE drawn as bricks (`[--][---][-]...`, 4-5 bricks each 2-6 wide drawn `[`+`-`*(w-2)+`]`, total width W in 14..20); line 2 is a number N (drawn from 2,3,3,4,4,6,6,7 - never 5, so that solve can always pick a height H in {5,6} with H != N and H-1 != N). SOLUTION = a wall built on that course: one line per course, TOP course first, every course a gapless tiling of the same width W by the same brick glyphs, at least 5 courses, the LAST line exactly the clue's first line, and exactly N TWIN STACKS. A twin stack is a brick sitting exactly on top of a brick with the same span (same left AND right edge) in the course directly below, counted over all adjacent course pairs. One clause a kid says in a breath: 'N bricks sit exactly on top of a brick the same size'. FOOTHOLD (measured, 500 fresh clues): a demo-less player reads 'build a wall on this course' straight off the clue; a random gapless wall on the clue course scores 9 % (5 courses), 13 % (6 courses), 14 % (5-8 courses) because N is drawn near the mode of the twin count of random walls. Stacked copies of the clue course score 0 % (4-5 bricks x >=4 junctions >= 16 twins, N <= 7 is unreachable), running bond 0 %, a constant wall 0.2 %, junk 0 %. Best rival family 'aligned joints = N' 17 %, 'clue row doubled then running bond' 16 %, 'one shared edge = N' 3 %, 'same-width pairs = N' 0 %. No template exceeds ~17 %; the rule scores 100 %. DEMOS: solve() ships 5-6 courses only (countable by eye) and rejection-filters every wall so that the twins are loud and the near-miss rivals are visibly falsified in the SAME picture: >=1 brick centred on a wider brick, >=1 brick of the same width offset by exactly one column, >=2 stray aligned joints (aligned joints that are not part of a twin), >=2 near-twins, >=2 one-edge-only pairs, and for N>=3 a triple stack (the same brick three courses high) plus >=2 twins wider than 2. Every count that could be mistaken for N - courses, junctions, total bricks, aligned joints, same-width-above pairs, near-twins, one-edge pairs, centred bricks, offset-by-one bricks, stray aligned joints, bricks in the top course, most bricks in a course, distinct widths used, width-2 bricks - is forced to differ from N in every shipped demo, so one demo kills the whole rival list at once. At least one twin always sits in the bottom junction, i.e. directly on a brick of the clue course, so the demo connects the picture to the clue. solve() randomises height, widths, which junctions carry the twins and all filler with random.Random(clue) and never emits the minimal witness.

def score(c,s):
 R=s.split();A=[]
 for r in R:
  b=re.findall(r"\[-{0,4}\]",r)
  if not b or "".join(b)!=r:return 0
  x=0;S=[]
  for t in b:x+=len(t);S+=[(x-len(t),x)]
  A+=[S]
 c=c.split()
 return int(len(A)>4 and R[-1]==c[0] and len({p[-1][1]for p in A})==1
  and sum(len(set(a)&set(b))for a,b in zip(A,A[1:]))==int(c[1]))
